description:
Welcome to ATLAS — Alert Tracking for Land-fire Activity & Safety 

I'm David Pirosmani, founder, volunteer, and adviser.

ATLAS converts NASA FIRMS (MODIS + VIIRS) satellite data into actionable wildfire intelligence. It provides hotspot tracking, fire-risk scoring, historical burn patterns, and a community alert network connecting hotspots with nearby village contacts.

Expertise: PHP/JavaScript/Leaflet/geospatial analytics, satellite data processing, bilingual (Thai/English) user experience design.
summary:
ATLAS (Alert Tracking for Land-fire Activity & Safety) is a live wildfire platform for northern Thailand built on NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS data.

Directly addressing the challenge, ATLAS harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS hot spots in one pipeline: it ingests both the near-real-time feed and the SP archive, deduplicates the same satellite overpasses by satellite, coordinates, date and time (NRT and SP serve identical detections with different file boundaries), merges detections into unified sensor categories — MODIS+VIIRS, VIIRS only, MODIS only — and clusters raw satellite pixels into ~1 km daily burn events a human can act on.

On this harmonized layer ATLAS adds decision tools: burn streaks (consecutive days a cell keeps burning), rule-based risk scoring (LOW/MID/HIGH with colored rings on the map), behavioral separation of technogenic sources from vegetation fires, and an alert chain that attaches the local administration's phones — village headman, subdistrict head, district office — to every hotspot, with crowdsourced, publicly auditable updates.

It matters because raw FIRMS output is thousands of points a day with no context; villagers facing fires rarely know whom to call. ATLAS turns the feed into an actionable, human-readable map — already working in production across months 2020–2026.
